text:
The best UK app-based bank depends on whether you want a full-featured daily account, automated budgeting, or maximum cashback and interest. Monzo is the best all-rounder for everyday spending and group expenses, Starling Bank wins for fee-free travel and traditional banking perks (like cheque imaging), and Chase UK is top for earning cashback on daily purchases.

Top UK App-Based Banks Compared
Bank	Best For	Key Everyday Perks	Foreign Card Spending	FSCS Protected?
Monzo	Social spending & budgeting	Instant notifications, bill splitting, "Pots" for organizing money, salary sorter	Free up to £200/month cash withdrawals (unlimited card spend)	Yes (up to £85,000)
Starling Bank	Travel & full current account features	Fee-free global ATM withdrawals, Spaces (saving goals), in-app cheque deposits, Post Office cash deposits	Unlimited free card spend and ATM withdrawals	Yes (up to £85,000)
Chase UK	Cashback & high-interest saving	1% cashback on everyday debit card spending (subject to monthly eligibility rules), round-up account, multiple virtual account numbers	Unlimited free card spend and Chase/JPMorgan ATMs abroad	Yes (up to £85,000)
Revolut	Multi-currency & investing	Hold and exchange 30+ currencies at interbank rates, disposable virtual cards, built-in crypto/stock trading	Free up to £1,000/month exchange (Mon–Fri) on Standard plan	Yes (received UK banking licence; verify account transition status)
Which One Fits Your Needs?

Choose Monzo if you share expenses: Features like Shared Tabs and Monzo.me (letting friends pay you back via a simple link without needing the app) make it the easiest option for splitting rent, dinners, or group trips. Note that its free tier limits fee-free foreign ATM withdrawals to £200 every 30 days.

Choose Starling if you travel often or still handle cash/cheques: Unlike most digital banks, Starling allows you to scan cheques directly in the app and deposit cash at any UK Post Office. It also offers unlimited fee-free ATM withdrawals abroad, making it superior to Monzo for heavy cash travelers.

Choose Chase UK if you want your current account to pay you: If you want to earn money back on groceries, fuel, and everyday bills without using a credit card, Chase’s debit card cashback and separate high-interest saver accounts provide the strongest financial return. Note that it does not support physical cheque or cash deposits.

Choose Revolut if you manage multiple currencies: While less suited as a primary UK salary account compared to Starling or Monzo, Revolut is unmatched if you frequently send money internationally, hold foreign currencies, or want disposable single-use virtual cards for safer online shopping.

How to Switch Easily

If you choose Monzo, Starling, or Chase, they all participate in the Current Account Switch Service (CASS). Once you open an account in the app, you can trigger a switch that automatically moves your balance, Direct Debits, and standing orders over from your old bank within 7 working days, closing your old account in the process. (Note: Revolut does not currently participate in CASS, meaning you would need to move Direct Debits manually).
